correctness.rationale: Lemma 1 (translation fixing for pairwise-coprime C): proof checked. Pairwise-coprime divisors of L have product dividing L by prime-exponent argument; CRT gives t with a_c+t=0 for all c in C; permutation x->x+t preserves density. Empirically confirmed on [7,8,9,10] (full 5040-combo optimum 1032/2520 equals C-fixed optimum). Lemma 2 (prime peeling): proof checked. Equivalence p prime with no multiples <=> p not dividing L0 holds because p|L0 iff p divides some m in S0. Lift counting uses gcd(L0,p)=1 so y+tL0 runs through all residues mod p; uncovered=(L0-c0)(p-1), D=D0+U0/p independent of a_p. Empirically confirmed on S0=[7,8,9,10] lifted by 11: all 11 residues give 12840/27720=107/231 as predicted. Iteration for distinct new primes valid as removal cannot create multiples. Lemma 3 (prime-max exchange): proof checked with one implicit step made explicit: any 9-set in [7,60] with prime max has max>=17 (7..13 contains only 7 numbers), while smallest unused m* in [7,24] is <=16 (7..16 contains 10 numbers), so m*<m_max; averaging argument Dmax(S')>=D0+U0/m* holds for any divisibility because for fixed S0 pattern each uncovered x is hit by exactly one of m* residues. Hence no optimal set has prime maximum. Union-bound maximizer 7..15 with sum 62575/72072 verified by Fraction; exchange by 1/m monotonicity valid. Witness densities verified by independent stdlib bytearray LCM enumeration: 36340/55440=1817/2772, 3290/5040=47/72, top-5 table rows match. Table completeness verified: 2002 distinct rows equal all C(14,9) subsets of [7,20], sorted descending. Core optima independently re-proved by a different branch-and-bound (union-bound pruning, no affine orbits): best core 3130/5040 (120960 combos brute-forced in 0.9s), runner-up 3290/5040 (2177280 combos in 15.3s), hardest 43M-combo core [8,9,10,12,14,15,16,18,20] proved 3140/5040 in 1.4s with 15783 nodes, 10-core random sample all optimal, and full 2002-set independent B&B in 106.4s found zero cases beating the table. Deterministic replay reproduce_census_7_20.py reran in 27.0s asserting best 1817/2772. Corollary interval for [7,60] follows rigorously from witness (lower) and union bound (upper). Machine-checked enumeration is experimental evidence with two independent implementations agreeing; lemmas are proofs.

originality.rationale: Live retrieval completed on 2026-09-07 via arXiv (single-paper and API) and Crossref (API + DOI). No prior maximal-density census for k=9, min>=7 in [7,20] or [7,60] was found. Nearest results compared substantively: (1) Hough 2015 arXiv:1307.0874 / Annals 2015 proves qualitative least-modulus bound (~1e16-1e18), concerns existence of full distinct coverings, gives no D*(9) value, witness, or LCM table. (2) Balister et al. Inventiones 2022 DOI 10.1007/s00222-021-01087-5 gives sieve/asymptotic bounds on density of uncovered set for large moduli, no exact reduced-fraction optimum or joint modulus+residue enumeration for nine moduli in [7,20]. (3) Zhang-Zhang arXiv:2607.19029 (2026) determines minimal LCM 10080 for a full distinct covering with minimum modulus 7, concerns complete coverings via filtering+Gurobi, not maximal density of incomplete 9-systems, and reports no 1817/2772 witness or 2002-row census. Crossref density query and arXiv distinct-covering query returned only these qualitative/full-covering works, no competing 1817/2772 or 47/72 table. Draft citation URL https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.09667 for Balister is erroneous (that ID resolves to a scheduling paper, verified live); correct Balister density paper is the Inventiones DOI above. This hygiene error does not create a novelty collision and is fixed in RESULT.md. Timestamp/memory/failed-search were not used to establish priority.

value.rationale: Independently worth finding later as a citable Erdős-benchmark number with reusable certificate, not a textbook restatement or parameter tweak. Textbook gives only Mirsky-Newman and 2,3,4,6,12 full covering (density 1, min<=2) and union bound 0.868; exact optimum 0.65548 requires handling overlaps and joint modulus+residue optimization, shown non-trivial by gap 0.002706 to runner-up 47/72 and by composite-beats-prime-heavy phenomenon (best union 0.8538 set is not best true density; 7..15 union 0.868 vs true 0.645). Stratum is principled: [7,60]x9 is first reciprocal-sum-impossible stratum (max sum 0.868<1), and [7,20] closure is the largest exactly closed sub-stratum (2002 sets, 544 cores) with honest limitation that full [7,60] (5.3B sets) remains open; prime-max elimination lemma is general reusable progress. Output is not an unexplained enumeration: divisor-lattice peeling + translation fixing + orbit/B&B method, reduced-fraction CRT replay in <2s, full deterministic replay in 27s, 2002-row table with residues and peel chains. Falls outside rejection classes: not mere substitution (threshold-justified), not tiny unmotivated gain (first exact table for min>=7 k=9), not bare dump (method + proofs + verifiers).

sources.comparison: Proves qualitative upper bound on least modulus of any distinct covering system (10^18 in arXiv abstract, 10^16 refined bound cited in draft; Annals 2015 pp.361-382). Concerns existence of full coverings only; computes no maximal covered density, gives no witness system or reduced-fraction density for k=9 with min>=7, and contains no 2002-row [7,20] census or LCM-enumeration certificate.
sources.title: Solution of the minimum modulus problem for covering systems (Hough 2015)

sources.comparison: Proves sieve and structural bounds on the density of the uncovered set for Erdős covering systems with large moduli (Inventiones 228, 377-414, 2022). Gives asymptotic/qualitative density estimates, not an exact joint modulus-plus-residue maximum over nine distinct moduli in [7,20]; contains no 1817/2772 witness, no 47/72 runner-up, and no divisor-lattice max-coverage table with CRT replay.
sources.title: On the Erdős covering problem: the density of the uncovered set (Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, Tiba 2022)

sources.comparison: Determines the minimum possible LCM (10080) of a full distinct covering system with minimum modulus 7, improving Klein 15120 via reciprocal-sum, divisor-completed IP, and Gurobi filters. Concerns complete coverings with min 7 only; does not study maximal density of incomplete 9-congruence systems, reports no uncovered-density optimum, and has no overlap with the 1817/2772 [7,20] optimum or prime-max exchange lemma.
sources.title: A Distinct Covering System with Minimum Modulus 7 and Minimal Least Common Multiple 10080 (Zhang & Zhang 2026)

residual_risks: Full [7,60] union-competitive counts (4008111 >0.65548, 612378 >0.70) were not independently re-enumerated (5.3B sets infeasible); they are motivational only and not needed for the [7,20] theorem or [7,60] interval.

Draft hierarchical affine-orbit correctness argument is terse; risk mitigated by full independent B&B re-proof of all 2002 optima (106s) and dual-method agreement on hardest core, but future reusers should rely on the B&B verifier and LCM checker, not solely the orbit code.
